citation: Lee & Li (2015), Kinematics, dynamics and control design of 4WIS4WID mobile robots
objective_model: Kinematic and Lagrangian dynamic model for four independently steered and driven wheels; 11-state formulation and trajectory controller.
limitations_relevance: Directly establishes that 4WIS/4WID kinematics and dynamics are already studied. No specific two-stage signed planetary transmission is the focus of the abstract/methods inspected.

citation: Zheng & Yang (2019), A Trajectory Tracking Control Strategy of 4WIS/4WID Electric Vehicle with Adaptation of Driving Conditions
objective_model: Three-degree-of-freedom vehicle model, tire-force distribution and hierarchical trajectory tracking under varied conditions.
limitations_relevance: Relevant on tire-force coupling and per-wheel actuator allocation; it means force distribution is not a novel contribution by itself.

citation: Jaskot, Posiadała & Śpiewak (2017), Dynamics modelling of the four-wheeled mobile platform
objective_model: Four-wheel platform dynamics for progressive/rotational motion with wheel slip and resistive forces.
validation: Numerical solution using fourth-order Runge-Kutta and prototype-oriented geometry; source description reports simulation results.
limitations_relevance: Shows four-wheel dynamics and slip are established topics; exact mechanical configuration differs.

citation: Hong, Velinsky & Feng (1999), Verification of a Wheeled Mobile Robot Dynamic Model and Control Ramifications
objective_model: Dynamic model with tire-ground interaction for a heavy differentially steered robot.
validation: Experimental data in loaded and unloaded conditions.
limitations_relevance: Not a swerve-drive platform, but a strong precedent for needing physical validation beyond dimensional checks or simulation.

citation: Seo, Moon & Kang (2026), Unified motion control of 4WIS-4WID WMR with unlimited steering and load transfer consideration
objective_model: Unified 4WIS/4WID controller accounting for tire slip, load transfer, Magic Formula friction constraints, and steering/drive allocation.
validation: Check publisher paper for its exact simulation/experimental scope before citing detailed performance claims; abstract inspected describes the framework.
limitations_relevance: Very close contemporary prior art on friction-constrained 4WIS/4WID modelling. Generic claims about coupling steering, tire forces and load transfer are not novel.

citation: Liu & Hashimoto (2026), Friction-Aware Force-Realizable Safety Control for Four-Wheel Independently Steered and Driven Mobile Robots
objective_model: Friction-aware safety control with torque constraints, conservative friction lower-bound estimation and force-realizable allocation.
validation: Numerical simulation study; article first published online 3 October 2026.
limitations_relevance: Current work on force/torque feasibility. Not a planetary transmission design paper but narrows the viable novelty of an integrated friction-feasibility claim.

citation: del Castillo (2002), The analytical expression of the efficiency of planetary gear trains
objective_model: Analytical procedures to derive efficiency expressions for planetary gear trains from speed/torque relations and power flow.
validation: Analytical derivation; inspect the full article before relying on a particular loss model.
limitations_relevance: Supports deriving the signed kinematics separately from efficiency. The constant 0.92 per stage in the design PDF is an assumption, not a verified operating-point efficiency.

citation: Talbot, Kahraman & Singh (2012), An Experimental Investigation of the Efficiency of Planetary Gear Sets
objective_model: Measured spin and mechanical losses in planetary gear sets across load, speed, planet count, roughness and oil-temperature conditions.
validation: Purpose-built test apparatus and measured power loss.
limitations_relevance: Indicates transmission efficiency depends on operating condition and hardware details; measure or calibrate it if precise power predictions are claimed.

citation: Nutakor et al. (2017), Planetary gear sets power loss modeling: Application to wind turbines
objective_model: Power-loss model including non-uniform planet load sharing, gear-mesh losses, bearing losses and lubricant drag.
validation: Compared predictions with previously published experimental measurements.
limitations_relevance: Provides a higher-fidelity alternative to a single fixed stage efficiency; application differs in scale and duty.

citation: Song & Byun (2004), Design and Control of a Four-Wheeled Omnidirectional Mobile Robot with Steerable Omnidirectional Wheels
objective_model: Kinematic/dynamic analysis of a steerable omnidirectional-wheel platform.
validation: Prototype and tests reported by the publisher abstract.
limitations_relevance: Related mobility literature, but steerable omniwheels are not conventional swerve modules; use only as adjacent context.
